sections.title: Reading Summary
sections.lead: You can use the spread to give your current question a clearer shape.
sections.text:
You can begin by naming what deserves attention in your current situation. A spread is an arrangement of positions, each giving a card a particular role in the reading. Orientation adds another angle, while your question determines which details are relevant. Neither feature ranks your worth or decides an outcome for you. Think of a new invitation: perhaps the useful question concerns available time, the kind of contact you want, or an expectation you have not discussed. Those are different questions even when they concern the same event. Try writing one sentence about what you want to understand before reading further. Keep it beside a note of what you actually observe afterwards. This gives you a way to use the reading thoughtfully and change your interpretation when circumstances become clearer.
Write down one observation you can check.

sections.title: Summary & Actions
sections.lead: For entertainment and reflection; this report does not replace professional advice.
sections.text:
Review one observation alongside the card description.
Use the theme to ask one specific question, then note what the response changes.
Record one relevant fact.
Ask one clear question.
Try a bounded adjustment.
This report presents traditional symbols as prompts for cultural exploration, entertainment and personal reflection. It describes possible tendencies within a symbolic framework rather than fixed outcomes or a measurement of your abilities. Your circumstances, choices and lived experience deserve more weight than a chart interpretation. When considering work, finances, [[term:health]] or relationships, gather practical information and seek qualified support when appropriate. You can use an idea here as a small experiment: choose a manageable action, observe how it feels and review whether it helps you. If it does not fit your situation, adjust it or set it aside. The report does not provide medical, legal or investment advice. Keep space for your own judgment, respectful conversations and new information as your situation changes. Cultural curiosity can accompany thoughtful decisions without deciding them for you. Daily scores, lucky indicators, and short action labels are also reflection prompts. You can check practical information before an important [[term:spread.decision]] and leave room around interpretations based on limited birth details.
